headline: Recommended not approving $231,635 police body-worn camera grant from state public safety office, 1-4 vote.
summary: Councilors discussed a $231,635 state grant for the Police Department's body-worn camera program. Some councilors raised concerns about ongoing costs and asked for more information. Councilors voted to recommend that the grant not be approved.
decisions: Recommended not approving the $231,635 grant from the Massachusetts Executive Office of Public Safety and Security to the Police Department for a body-worn camera program, by a vote of 1 in favor and 4 opposed.

8. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to accept and expend a $231,635 grant with no new

(ID # 26-0378 ) match required, from the Massachusetts Executive Office of Public Safety

and Security to the Police Department for a body-worn camera program.

Director of Intergovernmental Affairs (IGA) Nagim-Williams restated the request that the item be discharged from the finance committee meeting to be discussed in front of the whole council. IGA Director also added the administration’s willingness to have another meeting for discussion as

requested by Councilor’s. In response to Chair Wheeler’s suggestion to discharge the item without a recommendation Councilor Link shared

- opposition to the motion and the desire for more information. Councilor

Scott agreed with Councilor Link that it is the committee’s responsibility to make a recommendation on the item. Councilor Hardt spoke to the financial

burden of the item and did not want to recommend this item for approval at the rate of on-going costs.

Councilor Link moved for the previous question. The motion was approved on a roll call vote of 5 in favor (Councilors Link, Strezo, Hardt, Scott, Wheeler), 0 opposed.
